overall_summary: Markets are under clear pressure after a hawkish Fed hold, surging Treasury yields, and a sharp risk-off move in stocks. Escalating Middle East conflict, jumping oil prices, and weak Bitcoin ETF inflows add further headwinds for crypto. Near-term tone stays defensive until macro data and geopolitical risks stabilize.
key_points: Hawkish Fed hold and divided vote pressure risk assets
Middle East escalation and oil spike above $90
Bitcoin ETF inflows hit record monthly low
Morgan Stanley ETH and SOL ETPs offer limited offset

items.title: Fed Delivers Hawkish Hold; Bitcoin Holds Near $64K
items.summary: The Federal Reserve held rates at three and a half to three and three quarters percent in a nine-to-three vote, with three members dissenting for a hike. Chair Warsh struck a hawkish tone, saying there is no soft inflation target. Bitcoin barely budged near sixty-four thousand dollars even as stocks sold off and oil spiked on fresh Iran missile strikes and Trump's vow to hit back hard. Traders should care because September hike odds jumped and tighter liquidity remains a headwind, yet Bitcoin's hold of the sixty-three thousand support zone shows surprising resilience so far.
items.impact: Potential pressure if September hike firms; near-term range-bound if support holds

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Track Smallest Monthly Inflows on Record
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen just two hundred five million dollars in net inflows so far in July, the lowest monthly total ever according to SoSoValue data, with two trading days left. This follows billions in outflows in May and June. A modest thirty-two million dollar inflow on July twenty-nine snapped a multi-day outflow streak, led by BlackRock. Traders should watch this closely because thin institutional demand removes a key bid under Bitcoin and keeps the recovery fragile.
items.impact: Weaker structural demand may cap upside and increase downside vulnerability

items.title: Fed Whipsaw Liquidates $286 Million in Crypto Bets
items.summary: Bitcoin and ether price swings around the Fed decision wiped out roughly two hundred eighty-six million dollars in leveraged positions across nearly ninety thousand traders, even though prices finished the twenty-four hours almost flat near sixty-four thousand and nineteen hundred dollars. Longs took one hundred eighty-six million of the damage and shorts one hundred million. The bulk hit during the FOMC window. This matters because it flushes leverage from both sides and can set up cleaner moves once the dust settles, but it also shows how fragile crowded positioning remains.
items.impact: Leverage reset could reduce near-term volatility or enable sharper next directional move

items.title: Core Scientific Pays $42M to Exit Block Mining Deal
items.summary: Core Scientific recorded a forty-one point nine million dollar loss to terminate its bitcoin mining chip contract with Block and Proto, canceling future deliveries of about fifteen exahashes of 3-nanometer ASICs. The miner is accelerating its pivot to AI and high-performance computing colocation, which already makes up over eighty percent of revenue. Self-mining revenue plunged. Traders should note this as another signal that public miners are de-emphasizing pure bitcoin hashrate growth in favor of AI infrastructure, which could affect long-term network security narratives and miner stock correlation.
items.impact: Highlights mining-to-AI rotation; limited immediate BTC price effect but negative for pure-play mining sentiment

items.title: CLARITY Act Ethics Deal Nears as Recess Clock Ticks
items.summary: Senators Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego have finalized a revised ethics compromise for the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act aimed at winning more Democratic votes, according to sources, with language potentially heading to the White House soon. SEC Chair Paul Atkins has voiced strong support and said the agency is ready to issue its own crypto rules if Congress fails. Time is extremely tight before the August recess. This is important because passage would deliver long-sought market structure clarity and boost institutional confidence, but failure or delay keeps regulatory uncertainty hanging over the sector.
items.impact: Positive catalyst if it advances; continued overhang and possible SEC unilateral rules if stalled

items.title: Morgan Stanley Launches Cheap ETH and SOL ETPs
items.summary: Morgan Stanley Investment Management rolled out spot Ethereum and Solana exchange-traded products charging just fourteen basis points, the lowest fees in their categories, with staking rewards passed through to holders. The products expand the firm's crypto lineup beyond bitcoin. Launch volumes were modest but the branding and pricing matter. Traders should care because a major traditional finance name is deepening on-ramps for ether and solana, which can support flows into those assets and broader altcoin liquidity over time even if immediate volumes stay light.
items.impact: Supports institutional access and potential inflows into ETH and SOL

items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady in Divided 9-3 Vote
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.5 to 3.75 percent on Wednesday in a 9-3 decision, with three regional presidents dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike. New Chair Kevin Warsh emphasized the need to deliver price stability amid elevated inflation and Middle East uncertainty, without clear forward guidance. Crypto traders should watch closely because the hawkish dissents and lack of dovish tilt raise the odds of higher-for-longer rates or a future hike, which typically pressures risk assets.
items.impact: Supports elevated yields and cautious risk sentiment

items.title: 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits 19-Year High
items.summary: US long-term bond yields surged after the Fed decision and Warsh press conference, with the 30-year yield climbing above 5.2 percent to its highest level in nearly two decades. The 10-year also pushed higher near 4.7 percent as investors demanded more compensation for inflation and policy risks. Rising yields tighten financial conditions and often weigh on Bitcoin and equities by increasing the appeal of safer assets and raising discount rates.
items.impact: Tighter liquidity conditions headwind for risk assets

items.title: Stocks Plunge After Fed Hold and Warsh Comments
items.summary: Wall Street sold off sharply Wednesday, with the Dow tumbling more than 1,100 points or over 2 percent for its worst day in a year, while the S&P 500 fell about 1.5 percent and Nasdaq dropped around 1.7 percent. The reaction stemmed from the divided Fed vote, Warsh's inflation focus, and concurrent oil spikes from Middle East tensions. Equity weakness often spills into crypto, so traders need to gauge if risk-off extends into today's data.
items.impact: Risk-off tone pressures Bitcoin and related assets

items.title: Critical US Data Due Today: GDP, PCE, Claims
items.summary: Thursday brings the Q2 GDP advance estimate, June personal income and outlays report with the Fed's preferred core PCE inflation gauge, plus weekly initial jobless claims, all at 8:30 AM Eastern. Consensus expects GDP near 1.8 to 2.1 percent, core PCE easing modestly to around 0.2 percent month-over-month and 3.3 percent year-over-year. These prints will refine rate-path bets right after the Fed meeting and can drive sharp moves in yields, the dollar, and crypto.
items.impact: High-volatility catalyst for rates and risk assets

items.title: Dollar Steadies After Initial Softness Post-Fed
items.summary: The US dollar index dipped following the rate hold and Warsh remarks but found footing Thursday near 100.8, helped by geopolitical safe-haven flows from reported US air strikes in Iran. Mixed signals from the divided FOMC left markets unsure on the policy path. A firmer dollar typically acts as a headwind for Bitcoin priced in other currencies, so DXY direction remains key for crypto flows.
items.impact: Potential pressure on crypto if dollar strengthens further

items.title: Middle East Tensions Add to Macro Uncertainty
items.summary: The Fed statement explicitly cited elevated uncertainty from the Middle East conflict as a factor weighing on the outlook, while oil prices jumped on renewed Iran-related developments including reported US strikes. Higher energy costs risk feeding into sticky inflation and complicating the path for rates. Crypto traders should monitor oil and geopolitical headlines because they can quickly alter inflation expectations and risk appetite.
items.impact: Inflation upside risk supports tighter policy stance

items.title: US Hits Iran Hard After Missile Strike on Jordan Base
items.summary: Iran launched a surprise ballistic missile attack on a US base in Jordan that was intercepted, ending a brief pause in fighting. President Trump declared it was America's turn and the US carried out a heavy wave of strikes on IRGC targets across southern Iran including near the Strait of Hormuz. Traders should care because this restarts full hostilities in a five-month war that already disrupted global energy flows and keeps risk assets on edge.
items.impact: Heightened risk-off pressure and volatility across markets

items.title: Brent Crude Jumps Nearly 8 Percent Above 90 Dollars
items.summary: Oil prices surged sharply after the renewed US-Iran fighting and Trump's retaliation threats, with Brent closing up about 8 percent near 91 dollars a barrel. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains heavily depressed and Houthis are threatening more Saudi routes. Crypto traders need to watch this closely because energy shocks feed inflation fears, tighter financial conditions, and classic risk-off moves that often hit Bitcoin hard in the short term.
items.impact: Inflation and risk-off headwinds for equities and crypto

items.title: Drone Strikes US-Owned Tanker at Egyptian Port
items.summary: A drone hit a US-owned gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta Mediterranean port, sparking a fire that spread to a second vessel with no reported injuries. The attack comes right after the Jordan missile strike and US-Saudi responses, raising fears the conflict is spreading far beyond the Gulf. This matters for markets because it signals potential broader threats to energy infrastructure and shipping outside traditional chokepoints.
items.impact: Further energy supply fears and geopolitical risk premium

items.title: China Set to Deliver Air-Defense Missiles to Iran
items.summary: Reuters sources say Iran will receive the first shipment of up to 400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defense systems within weeks under a 60 to 70 million dollar deal. Trump said he would be quite disappointed if Xi follows through after earlier assurances. For traders this raises the odds of a prolonged war, deeper great-power friction, and more persistent oil and risk premiums.
items.impact: Prolonged conflict risk and US-China tension spillover

items.title: Senate Bill Gives Trump Huge New Tariff Powers
items.summary: A bipartisan Senate bill advanced that would let Trump slap up to 500 percent tariffs on Russian goods and as high as 100 percent on the biggest importers of Russian energy, with Iran elements also in play. It restores some trade authorities after earlier court losses and could hit China, India, and Europe. Markets hate the uncertainty this creates for global trade, supply chains, and inflation just as energy prices are already spiking.
items.impact: Trade uncertainty and potential higher import costs

items.title: Houthis Signal Major Escalation, Target Saudi Shipping
items.summary: Houthi leaders say the balance of power has shifted and they are ready for major escalation with Saudi Arabia while threatening ships and demanding fees in the Red Sea. This follows joint US-Saudi strikes on Iranian-backed militias in Iraq that killed IRGC officers. Combined with Hormuz disruptions it keeps dual energy chokepoints under threat and supports elevated oil prices and risk aversion.
items.impact: Sustained Red Sea and energy route disruptions
